short: The Den read and write: the den Queries, the write use case and its gate, and Zurfur's two Atta hosts
is: The den module: the `Den` namespace's two Query use cases (`root`, `node`) that turn a driver's path pieces into Atta segments and call Atta's resolver; Zurfur's type enum (`DenType`) with its per-type kind and content-not-shown facts; `DenThing`, the Account or commission an open node stands for; `DenHost`, the read implementation of `atta::Host`, which records every node it answers for, admits from that record alone, and dispatches each folder through one exhaustive match to the arm of the team that owns it (den's own top level and posts here; identity's and commission's arms in their own modules' `den.rs`). The write: `Den::write` (crate-private), every typed write's one door, which checks the pool's verdict, opens one unit, makes the grant from the locked standing (the system's from its own viewer-less locked read) and builds Atta's act from it; and `DenWriteHost`, the second `atta::Host`, which serves no read and applies each checked act through the gate, which runs each act's own domain rule on the facts its grant read before anything is written, lends each act's handler a view of its own whose one write lands the checked change exactly once, and builds the act's entry itself from the change that view recorded. Commission create, rename, the lifecycle move, the field acts and the system's Late mark are its real acts. Atta's types are imported only here; every public signature uses the application's own values.
conventions: Atta is imported only inside `src/den*`. The team arms (`user/den.rs`, `account/den.rs`, `character/den.rs`, `commission/den.rs`, `account/workflow/den.rs`) name Atta's values through `crate::den`'s re-exports.
Every miss is the one `DenError::NotFound`; the only other answer is `DenError::Store`. No arm, helper or Query panics, unwraps or expects; an impossible conversion makes the node absent.
A folder's real children and mounts are answered by the arm that owns the folder's place (`Place`); den's host matches over `Place` exhaustively, with no `_` arm.

`include_deleted` lives only in the host; Atta never sees it. The viewer comes from the session only (the system's is a fixed token no DID can equal), and every host method fails closed for any other viewer.
`admit` answers from the request's record alone: no store call, no failure.

The host keeps an arm's answer only when its place is a child of the folder's recorded place (`Place::is_child_of`) and, for `child`, its key is the key asked for; anything else is dropped unrecorded.

A place whose type doesn't show its content is closed: `child`, `children` and `mounts` below it answer nothing, so a listing and a typed path can't disagree. `/` and the top-level directories are traverse-only and list nothing. `/user/<did>` is looked up only for the session's own DID.

An open node's thing comes from the host's record for its real path, the recorded `Place` (`Place::thing`), in the same lookup as its soft-deleted word: no path segment is parsed for it, a mount carries its target's, and a card carries none.

The gate (`gate.rs`) is the only writer of node rows, the only issuer of a write capability and the only builder of a write's changelog entry: its free fn `gate` holds the crate's one `UnitOfWork::nodes()` call and `issue` the workspace's one `WriteCapability::gate_issued` call, each on its own `let` under its own `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`. `issue` is called only in `lend_as`; `lend_as` only in `lend` (once per leaf act, counted over `CommissionAct`'s production variants); and `RoleTable` is named, so implemented, only in `gate.rs`. `DenWriteHost::new` is named only in `write.rs`'s `written`, and `gate` only in `DenWriteHost::apply`. An act's `ENTRY` is exactly `EntryRule::Always(GatedEntry::NAME)` or `EntryRule::OnChange(GatedEntry::NAME)`, written out, and no two acts name the same gated entry; a `GatedEntry` (the kinds it may build paired with its own domain constructor, private fields) is built only in `act.rs`, each of its consts written out with its kinds and a constructor no other const shares; two constructors may build one kind. `tests/node_and_name_seams.rs` and `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` hold each of these.

A write is one unit: the node rows, the handler's write through its lent view and the gate's changelog entry land together or not at all. A refusal of any kind (Atta's, the gate's `DenRefusal`, a handler's) rides typed inside `Applied` and comes back as an `Err`, so the unit rolls back; a store failure is a `HostError`.
`Den::write`, its `Command` and `DenAct` stay crate-private (`write_gate_seams.rs` holds it): a driver reaches a write only through a typed use case that hands its act over and holds no unit.

An act's handler implements the gate's `Handler` (its `Role` marker, its `Checked` change, its `ENTRY` rule, its `precondition` with no default body, `handle`); who it needs (`Needs`: a create, a user's least role, or the system) is read from the marker's `RoleTable::NEEDS` through `needs::<H>()`, never written apart, and a thing anchor whose act needs a create fails closed; a user act refuses the system as its actor and the system's act refuses a user, on the pool and in the unit alike. The gate runs the act's `precondition` on the facts its grant carries for the role (`RoleTable::Facts`: an existing commission's `CommissionState`, read on the unit's connection after the lock; a create's `Unmade`; the system's `LateFacts`, its state and whether a `late` entry is still owed, read after its own lock) before it writes any row or issues any capability; a refusal is `DenRefusal::Precondition`, the unit rolls back, and the caller gets the rule's own answer. The handler is lent `&mut Lent<'_, H>`, a gate-owned view typed by its act, with private fields: every act's view holds `lent` (the capability's commission, read after the act's writes), and an act with a field write holds that one write on its own view only (`create` on the create's, `set_lifecycle` on the move's, `set_direction_status` on each direction act's, `set_deadline` on each deadline act's, `set_deadline_status` on each Delayed act's), taking no argument and writing the change the gate stored in the view, through the commission repo's method of its own name, with the capability and the stored change (as it is, or the port's value built from it by `From`); every method passes its own inner call through the latch, and a tripped latch fails the act whatever the handler answers. The system's act (`AsSystem`, whose `RoleTable::RECORD` is `Checked`) writes no field: no port method takes its capability, its view holds `lent` alone, and its entry records the change its rule checked, any write a broken rule; every other role's is `Landed`. The write is exactly once: it writes only a real change (a no-op writes and records nothing), by compare-and-set where the store holds the field, keeps its first answer, and a second call is a broken rule; when the rule checked a real change, an act whose write was never called, called twice or matched no row fails. `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` pins the surface (a generic impl of `Lent` or `View` holds `lent` only; each act's view its one write from a table of act → port method; each view write calls exactly its own port method with the capability and the stored change) and the latch over every item of `gate.rs`, inline modules included, and holds that nothing else there reaches the private fields of `Lent` or `View`: no module but `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` (a module there is a descendant and sees them), no `.view` or `.repo` outside an `impl View` or `impl Lent`, and no struct literal or pattern of either but in `lend_as`, which builds both, and `settle`, which takes both apart. The handler sees no unit, no changelog and no other repo method, and drafts no entry: the gate builds the act's one entry inside `lend_as`, while the capability lives, through the rule's gated entry (`GatedEntry::CREATED`: kind `Created` by `NewChangelogEntry::created`; `GatedEntry::RENAMED`: kind `Renamed` by `NewChangelogEntry::renamed`; `GatedEntry::LIFECYCLE_MOVED`: kind `LifecycleMoved` by `NewChangelogEntry::lifecycle_moved`; `STATUS_SET` and `STATUS_CLEARED`: kind `StatusChanged` by `direction_set` and `direction_cleared`; `DEADLINE_SET`: kind `DeadlineSet` or `DeadlineExtended` by `deadline_set`; `DEADLINE_CLEARED`: kind `DeadlineSet` by `deadline_cleared`; `DELAYED_SET` and `DELAYED_CLEARED`: kind `Delayed` by `delayed_set` and `delayed_cleared`; each from the change the view recorded), `Always` on every landing or `OnChange` only when the act changed a node row or its view's write landed, and refuses as a broken rule an entry of a kind its gated entry doesn't name, built on another commission than the grant's, by another actor than the grant's (an actor on the system's entry, none on a user's) or at another time, or carrying a note. A closure or a local fn can't be an act's entry: `EntryRule` carries a `GatedEntry`, whose fields only `act.rs` sees.

The handler answers `Handled { answer }`; the gate refuses an answer whose id isn't the grant's commission (or the minted id), and the answer leaves the write as `ArmAnswer` in `WriteResult`. A typed call builds its values from that answer plus the name and level the gate wrote; no node is read back.

No lint silencer in any production file of the use-case layer (`application/src`, the crate root and every module file included): no `allow` or `expect` of `dead_code`, `unused`, `unused_variables`, `unreachable_code` or `warnings`, outer, inner, under `cfg_attr`, in bodies and macro bodies, so none sits in the den, on a module above it, or in an act however its handler is written. An item no real act reaches is removed, never silenced; `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` (`no_production_source_holds_a_lint_silencer`) holds it.
An existing commission's grant is bound to the node its locked standing read answered: the walk refuses a top row that isn't that node as a store failure, so a write lands only on the bound node.

fs.name: access.rs
fs.role: den's access check: may this viewer open the node a read that bypasses the Den serves, named by typed ids; Atta's own resolve, open on exactly its real path, else the one not-found; the check keeps the plain walk and never tells equal names apart, pinned by access/tests.rs. Commission's download and changelog read call it; identity's reads (the viewer's own root, an Account) are next

fs.name: act.rs
fs.role: DenAct, the enum of every act the write carries (the commission's CommissionAct), its ActSpec (word, type, Anchor, Needs read from its capability's role: Create, Role(CommissionRole) or System, and ActShape: Create, Rename or Change, a field act on its node), BornEntry (a fixed word as key and name, a type, a picked level), EntryConstructor<C> (a gated kind's domain constructor: Bare, commission, actor and time in, or Change, the act's checked change C too, or System, the checked change and no actor; NewChangelogEntry out), GatedEntry<C> (the kinds it may build paired with its own domain constructor, private fields: the consts CREATED and RENAMED for any change, LIFECYCLE_MOVED over LifecycleMove, STATUS_SET over DirectionSet, STATUS_CLEARED over DirectionCleared, DEADLINE_SET over DeadlineSet, DEADLINE_CLEARED over DeadlineCleared, DELAYED_SET over DelayedSet, DELAYED_CLEARED over DelayedCleared and LATE over LateMark, the system's; builds() and construct(), which builds a Change constructor's entry only from a recorded change; and a cfg(test) for_test for the gate's misbuilt-entry tests), EntryRule<C> (Always a gated entry, or OnChange: one entry only when the act changed something), Handled (the handler's answer: the Commission its lent view read), ArmAnswer (that answer as it leaves the write, with a hand-written Debug that prints the id, never the owner's DID) and HandlerError (a store failure under the handler); act/tests.rs pins each bare gated entry's built entry (its own kind, the commission, actor and time given, an empty JSON object payload, no note), the lifecycle entry's literal payload from the move it is handed and none without one, and the rule's Always/OnChange answer

fs.name: admission.rs
fs.role: the admit table: live, archived and deactivated nodes by access, reach and include_deleted

fs.name: allowed.rs
fs.role: allowed_acts: what a viewer may do to one commission now, as the den's write would decide each act with nothing written: each act tried with the values `tried` names, an exhaustive match over CommissionActKind, so a new act fails to compile until the list tries it (every lifecycle step, every direction status, the rename to the shown title, a deadline at now as the set act stores it, each clear and Delayed act once; nothing of a create or the system's Late mark), each value judged through one `probe` by gate.rs's judge_act (the verdict on the role the act's capability needs, then its rule on the stored state at now), then write.rs's atta_passes (Atta's checks on the act the den's builder makes); an act listed, in CommissionActKind's order, when some value passes, a lifecycle target a step whose move changes the commission; ActWord (the act's word from its own spec), AllowedActs (the words in a fixed order, the targets); allowed/tests.rs: the values tried of every kind, against a second exhaustive match written apart (none of a create or the Late mark); on every lifecycle step × no deadline, one ahead, one past × the Delayed flag × the Owner and a Participant, each act listed exactly when one of its real calls lands on a fresh commission at that state (every value the list tries made for real, a deadline ahead and one past besides), each target exactly when its real move records a change, and some state listing every user act, counted from that second match; the order; no role lists nothing; archiving changes nothing

fs.name: authority.rs
fs.role: who may write where: `admit`, the pool's verdict before any unit opens (a top-level anchor by rule, only a create, only /commission; a commission by commission::den::pool_verdict), and `grant`, made inside the unit under the same rules: a user's from standing_for_update (user_grant), the system's from the viewer-less lock_for_system (system_grant, its one caller), each then reading the commission's row on the unit's connection (find), so its state is the locked row's latest, and the system's whether a `late` entry is still owed (late_owed); a user act refuses the system and the system's act a user, on both; a thing anchor whose act needs no role fails closed as WrongGrant on both; Grant (private fields, no Clone/Default, one private constructor plus a cfg(test) for_test; state_at_least answers the state to a role that suffices) over GrantKind (Existing commission+role+level bound to the node the locked read answered, carrying its CommissionState non-optionally, or Create under an id minted here by CommissionId::mint, v7, never the act's, or System commission+level bound to the node its lock answered, carrying its LateFacts, which only AsSystem issues from and existing_at_least never answers for); Grant holds the Actor, user() its user or None; cfg(test) MINT_AS plants the next minted id; authority/tests.rs: on the pool and in the unit, the fail-closed rule, the system's grant issuing no Owner's, Participant's or Creator's capability, a user act refusing the system and the system's act a user, the system's grant reading its facts under its own lock and a commission gone since the scan the one not-found, a rename with a top-level anchor refused, a place or top level with no arm the one not-found

fs.name: context.rs
fs.role: DenContext: the ports, the session viewer and the read's RootNaming (look up, or the cache only) every arm receives

fs.name: den_type.rs
fs.role: DenType, its 21 wire words, and the kind and content-not-shown tables; commission.brief and commission.participants are files whose content isn't shown, and unserved: no arm projects them, so nothing lists them

fs.name: gate.rs
fs.role: DenWriteHost, the write's atta::Host (serves no read, kind from type_kind, the unit in a Mutex read through get_mut, apply refuses another viewer) and the gate it runs once per act: grant kind, D-1 (nothing wider than Private until 0.6), then each act's rule, by `prepare` (an exhaustive match into Prepared, each a Passed: the handler and the change its precondition checked) on the facts RoleTable::facts reads off the grant, before any row or capability (a refusal is DenRefusal::Precondition), then the node rows walked from the grant's commission, its top row refused unless it is the node the grant is bound to, and written under the one `nodes()` binding (SegmentTaken recognised once; a rename to the stored name writes nothing; a change walks its node and writes no row; Written carries the node acted on or made and whether a row changed), then the act lent by `lend` (one `lend_as` per leaf act: create, rename, the lifecycle move, the direction set and clear, the deadline set and clear, the Delayed set and clear, the system's Late mark) to its Handler; RoleTable (Thing, Facts, NEEDS, RECORD, granted, facts, commission) for AsParticipant and AsOwner (CommissionState), Creator (Unmade) and AsSystem (LateFacts, its RECORD Checked: its entry records the change its rule checked, a write a broken rule), `needs::<H>()` reading who an act needs from its marker, `judge_act` (the gate's checks run with nothing written, for the acts list: an exhaustive match over CommissionAct, so a new act fails to compile until it is judged; each user act's arm the generic `judge`, private to the gate, the verdict on the role its capability needs, then its rule on a stored commission's state; a create and the Late mark Refused; answering a Judgement: Refused, Unchanged or Changes), grant_fits refusing every create and rename under the system's grant, `issue` (the one gate_issued call), `lend_as::<H>` (the one issue call: a Lent<H> over a View<H> holding the commission repo, the capability, the gate's node, the grant's actor, now and the checked change; then `settle` takes both apart: a tripped Latch fails the act whatever the handler answered, an answer naming another commission than the grant's is a broken rule, and `landed_once` refuses a checked change not written exactly once (never, twice, or a compare-and-set that matched no row); then, while the capability lives, built_entry builds the act's entry from the change the view recorded, as the rule says of what changed, refusing a kind its gated entry doesn't name, another commission, actor or time, or a note, and append_entry appends it in the unit); Lent's surface is create (the create's view only), set_lifecycle (the move's only), set_direction_status (each direction act's), set_deadline (each deadline act's), set_deadline_status (each Delayed act's) and lent (every act's), each through the latch; each view write takes no argument, writes the stored change once (a second call a broken rule, a no-op writing nothing) and keeps its first answer (Wrote); DenApplied carries the ArmAnswer, its Debug printing no name and no DID; refusals ride inside Applied, store failures as HostError; gate/tests.rs (with the gate/tests/spy.rs double over a real unit, which records each commission read and write by name, can redirect or fail commission reads, answer every lifecycle write as landed, and refuse appends): the role table, judge_act refusing a create and the Late mark to every standing, another viewer, a create through the write host, the latch on each adapter (a swallowing creator scripted on a view built by hand as lend_as builds it, then settled), a handler that writes twice and one that never writes a checked change failing on each adapter, a refused rule writing no row and lending nothing on each adapter, the move's entry carrying the change the view recorded, a deadline extension's legacy deadline_extended shape, a failed handler read, the answer check, the gate's node, owner and time, one created entry, the create's and the rename's entries with an empty payload and no note on each adapter, an entry built off the grant's commission, actor or time, of another kind or carrying a note a broken rule, a change constructor with no recorded change building nothing, an entry of another kind appending nothing on each adapter, the system's entry built by no actor and one by a user refused under the system's grant (and the system's under a user's), a role whose capability no write takes recording its checked change, one unit, no node read after a create's or a rename's writes on PostgreSQL

fs.name: host.rs
fs.role: DenHost, the one atta::Host for reads: the request record, the viewer check, the dispatch to each team's arm; its record answers each open node's soft-deleted word and thing; `found` names a node through names::display_name; `type_kind` is the one kind table every den host answers from (a type key the Den doesn't know is a file); `for_check` builds den's access check's host, whose reads name the viewer's root from the cache only; its apply is Atta's refusing default (host/tests.rs pins it)

fs.name: kind.rs
fs.role: NodeKind: directory, file, symlink

fs.name: level.rs
fs.role: atta_level, the one map from kernel's Level to Atta's, run in DenHost::found and the write's builder; den_level maps Atta's answer back for the output and the gate's rows

fs.name: name.rs
fs.role: DenName (From kernel's NodeName) and DenNameError: the Den's name rule, the write-side check every naming write calls and the re-check every read makes of the names Atta answers with; showable_refusal names kernel's ShowableName refusals (Account founding) in the same DenNameError

fs.name: name_ordinal.rs
fs.role: NameOrdinal and NameOrdinalError: the application's own number that tells equal names apart, over Atta's, 2 or more (TryFrom<u32>, From into u32)

fs.name: names.rs
fs.role: the fixed folder and entry words (a commission's six entries among them: attachments, products, slots, changelog, participants, brief), the id and DID keys (id_segment takes only the typed UUID ids, through the den trait UuidKey), the stored-text name with its `Unnamed` fallback, and display_name, the one place a name enters Atta (DisplayName::host_checked, banned everywhere else by application/clippy.toml, its #[expect] failing the gate if the ban stops matching)

fs.name: node.rs
fs.role: the `node` Query: a Den path below the viewer's root; after the plain walk succeeds, Atta's tell_apart numbers the node and its crumbs; node/tests.rs: per-viewer numbering, the archived twin, nothing stored

fs.name: output.rs
fs.role: the Queries' output values: DenNode, DenAccess (an open node's thing among its facts), DenCrumb (with its type), each DenNode and DenCrumb with its name_ordinal, DenListing, DenContent

fs.name: page_token.rs
fs.role: PageToken, the application's own token over Atta's, with FromStr/Display

fs.name: place.rs
fs.role: Place, Parent, TopLevel, Place::is_child_of, Place::thing (an Account's or a commission's directory names its id; every other place none), Node (an arm's answer), DenMount and the STANDING lift

fs.name: post.rs
fs.role: den's arm for /post/<did>: the empty posts stub, named `posts`, Public, the same for every DID; it takes no ports, so it reads no store and calls no host; nothing below it

fs.name: read.rs
fs.role: the Queries' shared read: path parsing, the viewer's root, the Reader over any atta::Host plus a RecordLookup (each open node's soft-deleted word and thing, in one lookup), Atta's answers into output values; each node's and crumb's name is re-checked by the Den's name rule on its way out, a refusal a store error whose text carries no name (read/proptests.rs walks stored text in through stored_name and out again); a crumb carries its entry's type, an unknown one a store error; Reader::tell_apart numbers a walked node and its crumbs, and every node and crumb carries Atta's number as its name_ordinal

fs.name: root.rs
fs.role: the `root` Query: the viewer's own root and its listing

fs.name: segment.rs
fs.role: DenSegment: one Den path piece in an answer

fs.name: soft_delete.rs
fs.role: SoftDelete: archived, deactivated

fs.name: state.rs
fs.role: NodeState: live, archived, deactivated (with whether the viewer is the Owner)

fs.name: test_acts.rs
fs.role: cfg(test) only: the real create, rename, lifecycle-move, six field acts and the system's Late mark as DenAct (create_act, rename_act, move_act, set_/clear_direction_act, set_/clear_deadline_act, set_/clear_delayed_act, mark_late_act), the system as an Actor (the_system), each field act's typed use case by one FieldCall (field_call), a commission's entries and fields read back (entries_of, fields_of), a stored commission's state at any step and with any field (state_at, state_with), a commission's real path, and Atta's acts built by hand around a real act's body (a rename onto any type at any path, a create keyed by any id at any picked level) for the tests that drive the write host below the den's builder

fs.name: thing.rs
fs.role: DenThing: the Account or commission an open node stands for, by its id

fs.name: write.rs
fs.role: the `write` use case (pub(crate), #[lazy_unit]): admit on the pool, open the unit, grant from the locked standing, the one builder of Atta's act, over a Target, private to write.rs (From<&Grant>: an existing commission at the locked read's level, or the minted id) (paths from the target's typed ids, an existing node's level from the target, a create's key from the minted id, each entry named by its word, a field act a Change on the targeted commission's node); atta_passes, the acts list's Atta check: the builder's act on an existing commission run through Writer::dry_run with its body dropped, no unit opened, Writer::act through DenWriteHost, both on den_writer's one Writer (the den's caps), so the list and the write meet the same checks; Actor (User(UserId), or System(SweepToken), which only commission/sweep.rs can make; its viewer the user's DID or a fixed token no DID can equal), Command, WriteResult (the thing, the name, the level and the handler's ArmAnswer; a hand-written Debug with no name and no DID), DenWriteError (NotFound, Forbidden, Refused(RefusalClass), Precondition(CommissionRefusal), the act's own rule's refusal, Store) and RefusalClass; write/tests.rs proves each rule on the real create, rename and field acts on memory, and the marked ones on PostgreSQL (the bound node, the no-op rename, one renamed entry, the grant binding the write, a stale move's and each stale direction, deadline and Delayed set's and clear's compare-and-set matching no row, each field act's one entry with its literal payload in its one unit through its use case, a move to the held step, a clear of nothing held and a set of the value held writing nothing, a dormant Delayed flag's clear landing on the stored flag and recording from, to and deadline null, a deadline set again one and two nanoseconds later, after 2000 and before 1970, running no deadline write and appending nothing, and a create's finer deadline held as the store holds it); write/log_tests.rs: eight writes at trace on PostgreSQL (renames, a create on a taken segment, the owner's move and one its rule refuses, a Delayed flag its rule refuses and a deadline set) log no identity at info, no name, no store detail; a create whose commission insert PostgreSQL refuses on its owner key, with a DETAIL naming the DID, is latched: the error keeps the DETAIL as its source, and no line at any level carries the DETAIL or a DID; the system's Late mark, landing and then owing nothing, logs no DID and no name at any level

notes: The identity arms (user, Account, Character) answer from slice 9; the commission arms from slice 10; the `/post/<did>` stub from slice 16, so a user's `posts` mount opens Public, its content not shown and its listing empty, and every path below it is the one not-found. The commission arms and the stub are also tested through the host from their real paths (`test_world::read`).

A folder's contents belong to the arm that owns its entries: a user's `commissions` folder and an Account's `commissions` folder are `CommissionPlace`s, and an Account's `workflows` folder is a `WorkflowPlace`, though identity answers each folder node as a child of its user or Account.
